retained_skill: Diagnose and repair an APT repository by rebuilding coherent package and release metadata so all supplied packages resolve through apt.
bottleneck: All 12 scored attempts reached repository publication but deleted or failed to regenerate InRelease; the verifier rejected otherwise usable repositories because it required that specific signing representation, although the instruction only requires a warning-free apt update and installability.
change: Repair the verifier only: accept the local repository being successfully fetched through either standard Release or InRelease publication, and remove the unstated requirement that an InRelease file exist and have a particular GPG representation. This is grading repair, not solver help; the original apt diagnostics remain the signal.
restore: Restore the prior direct InRelease/signature check and InRelease-only apt-output match after explicitly adding an InRelease deliverable to the public task, if that representation is intended to be part of the task.
prediction: The change addresses deletion or non-regeneration of InRelease after rebuilding Release metadata. It lets a student whose next action is to publish a standard apt-accepted Release repository receive credit, while still requiring apt to fetch the local repository cleanly and expose all packages. This is refuted if replayed detached-Release or trusted Release states still fail only because InRelease is absent, or if an untouched/no-op state passes.

evidence.observation: First representation error: removed InRelease instead of regenerating it. Replayed its trusted Release approach with all packages and graded it: six checks passed; only InRelease existence and InRelease-only fetch checks failed.
Removed InRelease after regenerating package metadata; later apt successfully installed all requested packages.
Removed stale InRelease and later reached successful package installation, leaving the same hidden representation mismatch.
Removed InRelease while replacing stale checksums; later made all packages apt-installable.
Removed InRelease at the signing stage rather than regenerating it.
Removed InRelease after inspecting it, then pursued an unsigned trusted Release repository.
Removed InRelease after rebuilding package metadata, matching the dominant first failure.
Explicitly removed InRelease and retained Release publication.
Removed InRelease and continued with Release metadata instead of the verifier's unstated required representation.
Copied unsigned Release content to InRelease, then removed it at turn 10; repository later supported package installation.

Removed InRelease, then generated a key and valid detached Release.gpg. Replayed that signed detached-Release approach from reset: apt update and package installation succeeded, six checks passed, and grading failed only the two InRelease-specific checks. After the verifier repair, the same approach replayed from a fresh reset and passed all seven retained checks.
Removed InRelease, rebuilt metadata, and installed all three packages; representative trusted-Release replay showed only the two InRelease-specific grading failures.
